_comment: Rules for the workspace pre-publish audit, run against whatever ref is
Use --worktree instead of --ref to audit tracked files as they stand.
`deny` holds strings the built-in patterns cannot know about, because they
look like ordinary words to a generic scanner: a provider brand host, an
M3U account suffix, a LAN prefix. Every pattern is written with a character
class so that this rules file does not itself become the leak it exists to
`allow` holds expected matches. Each needs a reason. Loosening a pattern to
silence a finding is how the next real one gets through: add an allow entry
Prove the rules fire before trusting a clean result. Plant a file containing
each forbidden string at a path that is actually scanned and confirm each
rule reports it. A gitignored canary proves nothing and looks like a pass.
The audit reads the CURRENT TREE only, while a push publishes every
reachable commit. Scan history separately with `git rev-list --objects`
plus `git cat-file -p` per blob against these same rules.

deny.why: the provider's real brand host, written as a pattern so this file does not contain it
the provider's real CDN host label in any form. Swapping only the top-level domain is not a placeholder: it still names the provider. Use edge-NN.example
the real M3U account name suffixes, one per provider login
this installation's LAN prefix, which names the operator's internal network
an operator-side backup path that appears in deploy notes and should not ship in plugin code or documentation
the operator's Windows workspace drive and path. The drive letter is separated by a character class so this rules file does not itself carry a Windows drive path

allow.reason: named in .gitignore so the working-notes file is never committed. The reference is the protection, not a leak: the file itself is excluded
the plugin's own install path inside the Dispatcharr container, documented deliberately in the README and the user guide
where the plugin writes its CSV exports, documented deliberately
tests/test_reports.py: documentary LAN address used as INPUT to the redaction test, which asserts it is removed from report text. Not this installation's address.
